meta.title: IT work archetypes: default role mix, productivity norms, three-point spread, complexity drivers and risk templates
meta.purpose: Bottom-up WBS seed data for the should-cost cockpit. Each archetype is a planning template, not a market price.
meta.currency_policy: No currency is embedded in the norms. Hours are currency-free; convert to RUB with rate_cards.json or contractor_rate_cards.json. No FX conversion.
meta.basis: Hours per unit of work. P50 is the most-likely value; O/M/P feed PERT and Monte Carlo.

provenance.licence_note: ISBSG-derived aggregate coefficients are cited, not raw ISBSG rows. ISBSG data cannot be redistributed without a distribution licence.

confidence_legend.High: The hours-per-unit is a directly published language/platform PDR (e.g. ISBSG low-code, ABAP, government median).
confidence_legend.Medium: Derived from a published PDR plus a small, explicit adjustment, or cross-checked against a published price anchor.
confidence_legend.Proxy: No direct public norm. Built from sourced components and an explicit planning assumption; calibrate before pricing.

meta.role_mix_policy: Default role mixes are planning templates derived from the project's integration example (research/10 section 2-L3) and professional judgement. They are NOT benchmarks. Replace them with the client's actual staffing plan.
meta.unit_policy: Do not sum hours across different units (FP, flow, report, bot, ticket, object, workload). Convert to hours first, then sum. Do not convert FP to CFP or story points without a local calibration (research/05 section 1.7).
meta.three_point_policy: P50 is the most likely value, not a statistical median. Use PERT for the mean and Monte Carlo for P50/P80/P90. Do not quote a single point.

recalibration.procedure: Replace p50_hours_per_unit and the O/M/P spread with the client's actuals for the same archetype; keep the role mix only if the actual staffing matches. If only total effort is known, back-solve hours per unit from the unit count.
recalibration.minimum_sample: 5-10 completed projects per archetype; report MMRE/MdMRE/PRED(25) (research/05 section 9.4).

confidence.High: The hours-per-unit is a directly published language/platform PDR (e.g. ISBSG low-code, ABAP, government median).
confidence.Medium: Derived from a published PDR plus a small, explicit adjustment, or cross-checked against a published price anchor.
confidence.Proxy: No direct public norm. Built from sourced components and an explicit planning assumption; calibrate before pricing.

meta.licence_note: ISBSG-derived aggregate coefficients are cited, not raw ISBSG rows. ISBSG data cannot be redistributed without a distribution licence.

archetypes.unit_definition: One end-to-end business flow with 2-6 message types, field mapping, error handling and monitoring.

productivity_basis.derivation: 10-20 FP/flow x 8.3 h/FP (ISBSG traditional median) = 83-166 h; P50 120 h is the midpoint of the derived interval.

complexity_drivers.effect: Multiple master-data objects and field mappings across two systems.
Inventory and warehouse errors are operationally visible.

archetypes.notes: Demo D1 in research/10 uses 6 flows and 930 person-hours; this archetype at 6 flows gives 720 h P50, before the integration-specific overhead captured in the D1 WBS. Use the WBS for a bid, not the archetype alone.

risk_templates.name: Scope creep / requirements volatility
risk_templates.mechanism: Requirements grow about 1% per month; 20-53% of original requirements change by completion (research/05 section 7.3).
risk_templates.mitigation: Change-control clause, REVL allowance, fixed-price boundary, re-baseline at gates.

risk_templates.name: Third-party API or schema instability
risk_templates.mechanism: Partner API changes, rate limits, undocumented behaviour or schema drift break integration (planning estimate).
risk_templates.mitigation: Contract tests, API version pinning, adapter layer, sandbox access, fallback batch.

risk_templates.name: Data quality / legacy data defects
risk_templates.mechanism: Legacy data is incomplete, duplicated or inconsistent; cleansing and reconciliation expand scope (planning estimate).
risk_templates.mitigation: Data profiling, cleansing sprint, reconciliation rules, acceptance data set.

risk_templates.name: Acceptance / warranty dispute
risk_templates.mechanism: Acceptance criteria are ambiguous; rework and holdback delay payment (research/05 section 7.4).
risk_templates.mitigation: Testable acceptance criteria, defect SLA, holdback, joint UAT sign-off.

archetypes.unit_definition: One unadjusted function point of a greenfield web application, including backend, frontend, tests and deployment.

productivity_basis.derivation: ISBSG Java median 8.7 h/FP; optimistic 3.2 h/FP is the ISBSG traditional P10; pessimistic 24.2 h/FP is the ISBSG Java P90.

archetypes.unit_definition: One KII object through categorization, documentation, protection measures and an acceptance audit.

productivity_basis.derivation: Categorization offers 55,000-277,800 RUB; at 3,860 RUB/h (the 15 case rate 100M/25,900 h) that is 14-72 h. A protection system starts at 900,000 RUB = about 233 h. A combined object budget of 160 h sits between the two; the anchor is a service price, not an effort study.

complexity_drivers.effect: FSTEC measures and KII category drive mandatory controls.

archetypes.notes: KII categorization is a small fixed-price service; a protection system is a project. Do not price both with one per-object norm.
